draft.title: Saving and interest
card: Interest is money a bank pays you for keeping your money in a savings account. The bank pays it because it can use your deposit to lend to others.
Interest is worked out as a percentage of your balance, called the interest rate. A higher rate or a bigger balance means more interest.
Simple interest
interest paid only on the original amount you saved.
Compound interest
interest paid on the original amount and on interest already earned. Savings grow faster over time this way.
draft.remember: Interest rewards saving, and compound interest grows savings faster.

a.q: Why does a bank pay interest to people who keep money in a savings account?
opts: It can use the deposits to lend to other people
It must give back more than customers put in
It wants to reduce the fees on customer accounts
It cannot hold the money without paying a charge
a.why: Banks lend out deposited money, so they pay interest to attract savers. The other options give reasons that do not explain why interest is paid.
a.clue: Think about what the bank does with the deposits.

b.q: Priya and Sam each save $1000 at the same rate for five years. Priya earns simple interest and Sam earns compound interest. What is true at the end?
opts: Sam has more, as he earned interest on interest
Priya has more, as she earned interest each year
They have the same, as the rate and amount match
Sam has more, as he started with a bigger balance
b.why: Sam's interest is added to his balance, so later interest is earned on interest as well. Priya earns only on the original $1000. The starting amounts were equal, so a bigger balance at the start is not the reason.
b.clue: Who earns interest on earlier interest?

a.best: It can use the deposits to lend to other people

b.best: Sam has more, as he earned interest on interest

problems.detail: The clue 'Who earns interest on earlier interest?' almost repeats the right option ('earned interest on interest'), so a student can match the words without knowing what compound interest is.
The clue 'Think about what the bank does with the deposits' points to the only option that mentions deposits, so a student can match the word instead of knowing the idea.

a.q: Why does a bank pay interest to people who keep money in a savings account?
opts: It can use the deposits to lend to other people
It is required by law to pay interest to every saver
It wants to reduce the fees on customer accounts
It cannot hold the money without paying a charge
a.why: A bank lends out the money saved with it, so it pays interest to attract savers. No law forces a bank to pay interest to every saver. The reason is that the bank can put the money to use.
a.clue: What can a bank do with money that sits in its accounts?
